:::{#def-rarity}
#### Rarity

The **rarity** of an [outcome](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-experiment-outcome) $x$
of a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) $X$
is the reciprocal of its [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) mass:

$$\rarityf{x} \eqdef \frac{1}{\P(X=x)}.$$

For a [continuous random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-continuous-rv) $X$
with [density](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pdf) $\p$,
the rarity of a value $x$ is the reciprocal of the density:

$$\rarityf{x} \eqdef \frac{1}{\p(x)}.$$

When the mass or the density is $0$, the rarity is $\infty$.

:::
